messages:
jamie_support: FYI billing issue from ACME (acct acme-123). Their daily CSV for 2026-11-02 shows ~12k tokens attributed to 2026-11-01 23:00 bucket instead of 2026-11-02 00:00. Invoice doesn't match dashboard. Attaching sample export link: https://files.redwood/acme-export-185
olivia_billing: Can you share the raw row? CSV snippet?
jamie_support: Here's the row from raw_export_shard_7.csv:
```
2026-11-01T23:00:00Z,acme-123,gen,token_count,12034
```
ryan_infra: That looks UTC. Did the aggregator apply local TZ somewhere?
mae_eng: usage-aggregator-v2 normalizes to UTC on ingest. If it's 23:00 UTC it should belong to that UTC day. Any timezone config on customer's side?
jamie_support: Customer claims their app expects day boundaries in US/Eastern. They expected tokens under 11/02. Dashboard uses account timezone = US/Eastern per profile.
olivia_billing: Aha — dashboard shows day-buckets by account tz, invoices use UTC-day buckets historically for billing (we changed to account tz in ui earlier). Could be mismatch.
alex_data: I'll query the ledger join between raw rows and billing rolls. Run:
```
SELECT r.row_ts, a.account_tz, b.invoice_day
FROM raw_usage r
JOIN accounts a ON r.account_id=a.id
JOIN billing_rollups b ON r.id=b.raw_id
WHERE r.account_id='acme-123' AND r.row_ts BETWEEN '2026-11-01' AND '2026-11-03';
```
alex_data: results: raw row 2026-11-01T23:00:00Z; account_tz = America/New_York; billing_day = 2026-11-01 (UTC day)
mae_eng: So invoice used UTC day, dashboard shifted to 11/02 (local) causing perceived missing day. Was there a migration that changed billing bucket logic around 2026-09?
ryan_infra: We deployed billing-rollup v3 on 2026-10-10 which switched to UTC for historical consistency. Frontend got an opt-in change to show account tz. Missed sync.
olivia_billing: Customer is charged correctly per invoices (UTC day). They see tokens on UI under 11/02, so they think invoice missing tokens for 11/02.
jamie_support: Customer wants either invoice aligned with UI or clear note. What are options for short term?
mae_eng: Short term: we can generate a per-account timezone-normalized CSV for their timeframe and attach as billing remediation. I can run a backfill job to produce this.
olivia_billing: Also need to log this as a usability bug. Customer-facing note + billing email + internal doc.
alex_data: I'll run one-off backfill job for acme-123 for 2026-10-30..2026-11-05. ETA 2h.
ryan_infra: Watch out for export-worker's TTL bug; last week worker 12 dropped rows when shifting buckets. I'll monitor.
support-bot: Reminder: create ticket BI-7654 and link to this thread.
jamie_support: Thanks. I'll message acme with proposed CSV and explanation. tagging @account-team to review copy :+1:
olivia_billing: Assigning to me for remediation communication. Update BI-7654 with invoice reconciliation steps.
jamie_support: Done — customer updates: they want an invoice-friendly CSV. Will send after Alex posts output.
alex_data: Backfill completed. Generated file: https://backfills.redwood/acme-123-2026-10-30_11-05.csv. I spot-checked counts: the per-invoice-day totals match invoice when using UTC buckets.
olivia_billing: Customer reply: they'd prefer invoice to match UI. This is a policy question. I'll escalate to pricing/ops.
mae_eng: For long-term, we should add note in UI when account tz != billing tz and consider migrating invoices to account tz with opt-in.
jamie_support: Closing loop with customer now. Tagging @ryan_infra to watch for similar reports.
ryan_infra: I'll add an alert that flags accounts with >5% diff between dashboard-day and invoice-day over 7d.
jamie_support: Great. Thanks everyone.
